relationships.title: Photosynthesis
relationships.description: The Sun provides energy for Flowers through photosynthesis, converting light into chemical energy that fuels plant growth.

relationships.title: Pollination Partnership
relationships.description: Bees pollinate Flowers as they collect nectar, transferring pollen between plants and enabling reproduction in exchange for food.

relationships.title: Water Cycle
relationships.description: Rain nourishes the Soil, replenishing groundwater and providing essential moisture for plant roots and soil organisms.

relationships.title: Oxygen Production
relationships.description: Trees produce Oxygen as a byproduct of photosynthesis, releasing it into the atmosphere and making life possible for animals.

relationships.title: Carbon Sequestration
relationships.description: Trees absorb Carbon Dioxide from the atmosphere, using it for photosynthesis and helping regulate Earth's climate.

relationships.title: Nature's Recyclers
relationships.description: Mushrooms act as Decomposers, breaking down dead organic matter and returning nutrients to the soil for new life.

relationships.title: Nutrient Cycling
relationships.description: Decomposers enrich the Soil by breaking down organic matter into nutrients that plants can absorb and use for growth.

relationships.title: Seed Dispersal
relationships.description: Birds disperse Seeds by eating fruits and depositing them far from the parent plant, helping forests spread and regenerate.

relationships.title: Water Source
relationships.description: Rivers sustain Forests by providing a constant water source, creating riparian ecosystems rich in biodiversity.

relationships.title: Atmospheric Moisture
relationships.description: Forests generate Rain through transpiration, releasing water vapor that forms clouds and creates local rainfall patterns.

relationships.title: Life Cycle
relationships.description: Seeds grow into Trees when conditions are right, beginning the cycle of life that can last for hundreds of years.

relationships.title: Root System
relationships.description: Soil anchors Trees through their root systems, providing stability and a medium for nutrient and water absorption.

relationships.title: Food Chain
relationships.description: Predators hunt Birds as part of the natural food chain, maintaining population balance in the ecosystem.

relationships.title: Reproduction
relationships.description: Flowers produce Seeds after pollination, ensuring the next generation of plants can spread and colonize new areas.

relationships.title: Evaporation Cycle
relationships.description: The Sun creates Rain by evaporating water from oceans and land, which rises, cools, and falls back to Earth.

relationships.title: Pollinator Habitat
relationships.description: Bees inhabit Forests, finding shelter in tree hollows and pollinating countless plant species throughout the woodland.

relationships.title: Mycorrhizal Network
relationships.description: Mushrooms form symbiotic relationships with Trees through underground fungal networks, exchanging nutrients and information.

relationships.title: Atmospheric Balance
relationships.description: Oxygen and Carbon Dioxide balance each other in Earth's atmosphere through the respiration and photosynthesis cycles.

relationships.title: Sediment Transport
relationships.description: Rivers deposit nutrient-rich Soil along their banks during floods, creating fertile floodplains for plant growth.

relationships.title: Death and Decay
relationships.description: When Predators die, Decomposers break down their bodies, completing the nutrient cycle and returning energy to the ecosystem.
